legacy_root.title: Assess keyless signing (Sigstore/cosign) applicability to a file-based plugin marketplace
legacy_root.question: Can a marketplace whose packages are directories of markdown and scripts obtain a meaningful keyless signature, what exactly does the signature attest to, and what does it NOT prevent?
legacy_root.answer: Yes, with a scoped meaning. Hash the plugin directory to a canonical tree digest and keyless-sign that blob (or emit a DSSE in-toto attestation whose subject is that digest), then verify with a pinned GitHub Actions / OIDC identity. The signature attests identity + digest + Rekor witness. It does not prevent signed malware in SKILL.md, unpinned-identity spoofing, OIDC/CI compromise, partial-tree substitution, or runtime fetches of unsigned bytes.

marketplace_applicability.package_shape: directories of markdown and scripts (plugin.json + SKILL.md + scripts)

does_not_cover: Fulcio chain validation against the Sigstore TUF trust root
Rekor Merkle inclusion-proof recomputation against the Signed Tree Head
Semantic inspection of wheel / markdown / script contents

does_not_prevent.attack: Publisher (or anyone who controls the pinned GitHub workflow) ships a SKILL.md with prompt injection / data-exfil instructions. Keyless verify succeeds because the digest is honest.
does_not_prevent.why_signature_does_not_stop_it: The verified sampleproject statement predicate is JSON null; the subject is only filename+sha256. Cosign/DSSE never parse markdown.

does_not_prevent.attack: Marketplace install gate checks only that a Sigstore signature verifies, not that certificate-identity matches the expected publisher workflow.
does_not_prevent.why_signature_does_not_stop_it: The same real ECDSA-verified attestation is accepted by a naive policy and rejected when the expected identity is pinned to an unrelated workflow URI.

does_not_prevent.attack: Sign only plugin.json (or a subset of files). Adversary replaces SKILL.md / scripts after signing.
does_not_prevent.why_signature_does_not_stop_it: plugin.json-only digest is identical for clean vs swapped trees; the full-tree digest is not.

does_not_prevent.attack: Stolen GitHub Actions OIDC token or compromised workflow YAML lets an attacker obtain a Fulcio cert for the expected identity.
does_not_prevent.why_signature_does_not_stop_it: Sigstore's own security model states that a compromised OIDC identity can yield unauthorized certificates; detection depends on log monitoring, not on the signature check itself.
does_not_prevent.demonstration_class: vendor-documented residual, not a local forge

does_not_prevent.attack: A signed script downloads and execs unsigned content after install-time verify has already passed.
does_not_prevent.why_signature_does_not_stop_it: sign-blob / DSSE bind bytes that existed at signing time. Runtime network fetches are outside the digest.

mitigations.claim: Rejecting marketplace packages that lack any valid Sigstore signature is sufficient.
mitigations.bypass_attempt: Feed the real pypa/sampleproject attestation to a marketplace that expected a different publisher. A signature-exists-only gate accepts it; an identity-pinned gate rejects it.
mitigations.residual: Any GitHub Actions identity that can talk to Fulcio produces an equally valid keyless signature.

mitigations.claim: cosign verify-blob / DSSE verify of a canonical tree digest with --certificate-identity and --certificate-oidc-issuer pinned to the publisher workflow stops third-party substitution of files after signing.
mitigations.bypass_attempt: Swap skills/skill.demo/SKILL.md after the tree digest is taken. Full-tree digest changes; a pinned verify of the original digest would fail. Bypass of substitution: failed.
mitigations.residual: Does not stop the pinned identity from signing malware, a compromised GitHub Actions token, or a signed script that fetches unsigned bytes at runtime.

mitigations.claim: A valid keyless signature means the markdown/scripts are safe.
mitigations.bypass_attempt: Build a plugin tree whose SKILL.md contains prompt-injection and an exfiltration instruction. The tree still has a well-formed digest; the verified PyPI publish attestation has predicate=null and never inspects file semantics.

claims.claim: Yes: a marketplace whose packages are directories of markdown and scripts can obtain a meaningful keyless signature by first hashing the directory into one blob (canonical sorted sha256+path manifest) and then applying Sigstore keyless sign-blob / a DSSE in-toto attestation over that digest, the same binding PyPI already uses for a wheel file.
claims.strongest_caveat: Meaningful only if the verifier pins identity and hashes the entire installable tree, not a subset.

rails.observation: PyPI Integrity API returned a PEP 740 provenance object whose in-toto subject is filename+sha256=c23e447ea90d796d1e645c35c4b2de125040add12a845825546f91c93f391b6b; live wheel bytes hash to that digest. The attested object is a file blob, which is the same shape as a directory manifest blob.

Official Cosign docs: keyless sign-blob signs standard files/blobs and stores signature, certificate, and Rekor inclusion in a bundle. Quote:  process as "keyless signing". You use `cosign sign-blob` to sign standard files as well as blobs. You can store signature and certificate information either as separate file, or in a bundled text file, but using a bundl

claims.claim: The keyless signature attests that an OIDC identity (here the GitHub Actions workflow URI plus issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com) bound an ephemeral key via a short-lived Fulcio certificate and signed a specific digest, and that a Rekor dsse entry witnessed that payload hash. It does not attest that the bytes are safe, correct, or complete as a product.
claims.strongest_caveat: This probe verified the leaf signature and identity extraction; it did not re-walk the Fulcio chain against the Sigstore TUF trust root.

rails.observation: ECDSA-SHA256 over DSSE PAE verified with the Fulcio leaf public key. SAN URI=https://github.com/pypa/sampleproject/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main; issuer OID=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com; cert window 2024-11-06T22:37:07Z .. 2024-11-06T22:47:07Z; publish/v1 predicate is JSON null.

Sigstore overview: keyless signing associates identities, rather than keys, with an artifact signature; Fulcio binds an ephemeral key to an OIDC identity; Rekor records a timestamped hash+key+signature tuple. Quote: ificate_authority/oidc-in-fulcio">}}).  Keyless signing associates identities, rather than keys, with an artifact signature. Fulcio issues short-lived certificates binding an ephemeral key to an OpenID Connect identity.

claims.claim: A verifier that only checks 'a Sigstore signature verifies' is not a marketplace trust signal. Cosign requires --certificate-identity and --certificate-oidc-issuer; the same real sampleproject signature is accepted by a naive signature-exists policy and rejected when the expected identity is pinned to an unrelated workflow.
claims.strongest_caveat: Pinning the workflow URI at refs/heads/main still allows later commits on main to sign; pin the workflow digest for a tighter bind.

rails.observation: The Fulcio SAN matches the workflow file at commit 621e4974ca25ce531773def586ba3ed8e736b3fc, which sets id-token: write for Trusted Publishing. Mechanical control: naive_accepts=True pinned_real=True pinned_wrong=False.

OIDC verification cheat sheet: GitHub Actions identity is the workflow URI@ref and issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com. Both fields are required. claims.claim: Rekor logIndex 147137144 is a dsse kind entry whose payloadHash equals sha256 of the attested in-toto statement; a GET of that index from rekor.sigstore.dev still returns the same payload hash.
claims.strongest_caveat: Inclusion-proof hashes were captured but not recomputed against the Signed Tree Head in this unit.

Sigstore security model: Rekor is an append-only transparency log; an entry is a single-party attestation that data existed prior to a time. Quote: imestamp.  An entry in Rekor provides a single-party attestation that a piece of data existed prior to a certain time. claims.claim: The signature does not inspect markdown or scripts. The verified publish/v1 statement has predicate=null, and a plugin tree whose SKILL.md contains prompt-injection still has a well-formed canonical digest that would verify if signed by the pinned identity.
claims.strongest_caveat: Content scanning is a different control, not Sigstore.

rails.observation: Decoded in-toto statement predicate is JSON null; subject is only name+sha256. Malicious fixture tree digest f7033074e332d72099456f47744b7183a14954d6f3555fa908a0583e0a4b410e differs from clean b7b91e98fbe944b07b762299ec1b9f573896898fd2fb93cc189204bc9b63a1ba but both are valid digest inputs to sign-blob.

Rekor inclusion proof hashes captured, not recomputed
No local keyless signing was performed (no OIDC token); verification used a production PyPI/Sigstore attestation
